rationale: Four patch findings remain: Windows cmd.exe mis-quoting in the pre-commit secret scanner that may silently skip gitleaks (CR-001), a false 'restore failed' banner shown after an explicit workflow stop before any content streamed (CR-003), empty-tabs URL param never cleared when all ES-gated flags are off (CR-002), and a lagging-GET race window that transiently re-marks an empty-response workflow turn as in-progress (CR-004). One pre-existing finding deferred (missing isWorkflow guard in hasInProgressExecution, predates this change — see code-review-deferred.md); 5 dismissed as noise. No spec/story ArtifactRef was available; acceptance lenses did not run.

standards_review.notes: All 7 subjects match the documented EPMCDME-XXXX: Capital sentence pattern with non-zero ticket IDs. Branch name uses a hyphen separator instead of the documented underscore pattern; commit-format check covers subjects only.
No guide found at .ai-run/guides/standards/code-quality.md and no ArtifactRef supplied; absent standard.

No dangerouslySetInnerHTML sinks introduced. No navigation built from untrusted URL input. No cross-window message handlers added. FEATURE_FLAGS constants contain no secrets. .mcp.json added to .gitignore is positive hygiene. No secrets placed in VITE_* or window._env_ config.

findings.title: quoteForShell misquotes on Windows cmd.exe
findings.problem: quoteForShell escapes embedded double-quotes as \" and does not double trailing backslashes before the closing quote. cmd.exe treats \" as an escaped quote rather than a string delimiter, and a path ending in \ causes the closing " to be consumed as an escape, leaving the argument unclosed.
findings.impact: On Windows, a project path that contains an embedded double-quote or ends with a backslash produces malformed arguments for the gitleaks spawn. Gitleaks may receive no valid scan path and exit 0 without scanning, silently bypassing the pre-commit secret check for that developer.
findings.recommendation: Replace value.replace(/"/g, '\\"') with value.replace(/"/g, '""') to use the cmd.exe-correct doubling escape, and add value = value.replace(/\\+$/, m => m + m) before wrapping in quotes to double any trailing backslashes.

findings.title: Empty tab list skips stale URL cleanup
findings.problem: The useEffect URL-fallback at line 163 returns early when isMetricsAnalyticsLoaded is false, then redirects only when tabs.length > 0 and the active tab is not found. When all ES-gated flags are off, tabs is always empty, so tabs.length > 0 is permanently false and the redirect branch never executes.
findings.impact: A user with all analytics feature flags disabled navigates to the Analytics page with a stale ?tab=foo URL. The tab bar renders empty via alwaysShowTabs={true}, the content area is blank, and the URL stays on the unresolvable tab ID indefinitely with no user-visible recovery.
findings.recommendation: Add an else branch (or a second condition) inside the useEffect: when isMetricsAnalyticsLoaded is true and tabs.length === 0, call setSearchParams to delete the tab param — e.g. next.delete('tab') — with replace: true, to clear the stale value.

findings.title: False restore-failed banner after explicit workflow stop
findings.problem: showRestoreFailed (line 183) has no guard for message.generationStopped. When stopChatGeneration aborts a workflow turn before any content is streamed, it sets generationStopped=true, inProgress=false, drops thoughts, and calls stream.finish() without nulling the stream. markdownContent then resolves to stream.getStream() (empty) ?? response (empty), making all conditions true and firing the banner.
findings.impact: A user who clicks Stop on a workflow before the first response chunk sees 'Workflow progress could not be restored.' immediately after stopping, rather than a blank/silent turn. The message is factually wrong — the user stopped intentionally, not because of a reload failure — and undermines trust in the workflow status display.
findings.recommendation: Add !message.generationStopped && to the showRestoreFailed compound condition alongside the existing !isInProgress check. This is the same field stopChatGeneration sets and _handleGenerationAbort propagates for workflow turns.

findings.title: Lagging GET re-enables inProgress for empty-response turn
findings.problem: refreshWorkflowExecutionIds guards against lagging GETs at line 262 only when the local message already has a response (existingMessage.response && !message.response). A turn whose stream closed with no content has existingMessage.response = null; the guard does not fire, and line 268 unconditionally writes existingMessage.inProgress = message.inProgress. A lagging GET that still carries inProgress: true re-marks the locally-finished turn as in-progress.
findings.impact: On a workflow turn that produces no text before the stream closes, a lagging poll response transiently re-activates the polling loop and may briefly re-render progress UI or delay the terminal status. Subsequent polls self-correct, but the window is a fragile assumption left unguarded by the existing comment at line 260.
findings.recommendation: Widen the guard before line 268 to cover the empty-local-response case: add if (existingMessage.generationStopped || !message.inProgress) return before the unconditional inProgress write, or check !existingMessage.inProgress && message.inProgress explicitly and skip the write, so a lagging in-progress server response can never re-mark a locally-finished turn.
